rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship on an edge is insecure doubt; the metaphor is someone unstable on an edge. Gratitude in ease and patience in hardship would make worship firm.
rows.anchor: على شك وأصله من حرف الشيء وهو طرفه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: The person is a hypocrite, worshipping with the tongue rather than the heart.
rows.anchor: هو المنافق يعبده بلسانه دون قلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good fortune is health and ample livelihood, which reassures him; bodily affliction or constrained livelihood makes him apostatize. He loses worldly hopes and the Hereafter through loss of religion and eternal Hell.
rows.anchor: صحة في جسمه، وسعة في معيشته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaʿqūb reads خاسر with an alif and reads الآخرة in the genitive; خسران مبين means manifest loss.
rows.anchor: قرأ يعقوب " خاسر " بالألف {والآخرة} جر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أعوذ means I seek protection; hamazāt are explained as incitements, whispers, blowing and spitting, or driving people to sin. Hamz originally means forceful pushing.
rows.anchor: وأصل الهمز شدة الدفع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The devils’ hamazāt are their incitements.
rows.anchor: نزعاتهم. وقال الحسن: وساوسهم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: The devils’ hamazāt are their whisperings.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: وساوسهم. وقال مجاهد

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: The devils’ hamazāt are their blowing and spitting.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: نفخهم ونفثهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer asks that devils not attend any affair, because their presence prompts whispering.
rows.anchor: لأن الشيطان إذا حضره يوسوسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers who deny resurrection ask to return to the world when they see death.
rows.anchor: يسألون الرجعة إلى الدنيا عند معاينة الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ارجعون uses an honorific plural to address God alone, as Arabs address one person in the plural.
rows.anchor: فإنهم يخاطبون الواحد بلفظ الجمع على وجه التعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural resembles God’s own إنا نحن wording.
rows.anchor: إنا نحن نزلنا الذكر وإنا له لحافظون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative is that, after appealing to God, the dying person turns to the angels taking his soul and asks them to return him.
rows.anchor: الملائكة الذين يقبضون روحه ابتداء بخطاب الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says he wants to make up the neglected testimony that there is no god but God; another view is that he wants to obey God.
rows.anchor: ضيعت أن أقول لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He wants neither family nor worldly wealth and pleasures; he wishes to return only to obey God.
rows.anchor: ما تمنى أن يرجع إلى أهله وعشيرته ولا ليجمع الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كلا rebukes the request: he will not return; it is merely a word he says and will not obtain.
rows.anchor: كلمة ردع وزجر، أي: لا يرجع إليها

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Barzakh is a barrier preventing return to worldly life.
rows.anchor: حجاب بينهم وبين الرجوع إلى الدنيا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Barzakh means the remainder of worldly life.
rows.anchor: بقية الدنيا

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Barzakh is the span from death to resurrection.
rows.anchor: ما بين الموت إلى البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation identifies barzakh as the grave, where they remain until resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو القبر، وهم فيه إلى يوم يبعثون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He identifies this as the first blast; they fall unconscious, then rise after the next blast and converse.
rows.anchor: أنها النفخة الأولى

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: He identifies it as the second blast; people are summoned to settle rights even against relatives, so lineage offers no protection.
rows.anchor: يؤخذ بيد العبد والأمة يوم القيامة فينصب على رءوس الأولين والآخرين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In ʿAṭāʾ’s transmission it is the second blast; people do not boast of lineage or ask social introductions, though kinship itself remains.
rows.anchor: فلا أنساب بينهم أي: لا يتفاخرون بالأنساب يومئذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report that every bond and lineage ends except the Prophet’s is explained as faith and Qur’an being his surviving bond and lineage.
rows.anchor: يوم القيامة سبب ولا نسب إلا نسبه وسببه، وهو الإيمان والقرآن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The apparent contrast with people conversing elsewhere is resolved by different stages: terror silences them in one place; they recover and converse in another.
rows.anchor: أن للقيامة أحوالا ومواطن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those whose scales weigh heavily are successful.
rows.anchor: فمن ثقلت موازينه فأولئك هم المفلحون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those whose scales are light have lost themselves and remain in Hell.
rows.anchor: خسروا أنفسهم في جهنم خالدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Talfah means the fire scorches or burns their faces; kāliḥūn means frowning.
rows.anchor: تلفح وجوههم النار} أي: تسفع، وقيل: تحرق، {وهم فيها كالحون} عابسون

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: The Prophet describes the fire drawing the upper lip to the head’s middle and loosening the lower lip to the navel.
rows.anchor: فتقلص شفته العليا حتى تبلغ وسط رأسه، وتسترخي شفته السفلى

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The disbeliever grows to the size of a seven-night journey in the Fire, with a molar like Mount Uḥud and lips at the navel.
rows.anchor: يعظم الكافر في النار مسيرة سبع ليال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs recited to them mean the Qur’an, by which they were warned.
rows.anchor: يعني القرآن، تخوفون بها، {فكنتم بها تكذبون}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read شقاوتنا with alif and fatḥa; both forms are dialectal, and they blame a written destiny for their misguidance.
rows.anchor: بالألف وفتح الشين، وهما لغتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: اخسؤوا means be driven away, as an order used to repel a dog; God will not lift their punishment and they despair.
rows.anchor: في رفع العذاب، فإني لا أرفعه عنكم، فعند ذلك أيس المساكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read قل as an imperative addressing the group or each disbeliever; others read قال in both places. Ibn Kathīr also reads the imperative.
rows.anchor: على الأمر. ومعنى الآية: قولوا أيها الكافرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question concerns years in this world and graves; torment makes them forget the duration, so they answer a day or part of a day.
rows.anchor: أي: في الدنيا وفي القبور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “reckoners” are angels who preserve and count human deeds.
rows.anchor: الملائكة الذين يحفظون أعمال بني آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their stay was little compared with the Hereafter, since worldly and grave residence is finite.
rows.anchor: لأن لبثه في الدنيا وفي القبر متناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God did not create people pointlessly or without wisdom; against an alternative reading of creation for play like animals, the author says they were created to worship and obey God.
rows.anchor: وإنما خلقتم للعبادة وإقامة أوامر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse rejects no return for recompense; Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Yaʿqūb read تُرجعون with fatḥa on tāʾ and kasra on jīm.
rows.anchor: لا ترجعون في الآخرة للجزاء

rows.speaker: حنش
rows.claim: A man with an affliction was healed after Ibn Masʿūd recited the verse through the sūrah; the Prophet said a certain believer’s recitation could move a mountain.
rows.anchor: أن رجلا مصابا مر به على ابن مسعود فرقاه

rows.speaker: محمد
rows.claim: The Prophet says that a person of certainty could recite this sūrah over a mountain and make it move.
rows.anchor: لو أن رجلا موقنا قرأها على جبل لزال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Birds are singled out because they occupy the space between heaven and earth, outside the categories in either.
rows.anchor: لأنها تكون بين السماء والأرض فتكون خارجة عن حكم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Prayer belongs to people; other creatures glorify God.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: الصلاة لبني آدم، والتسبيح لسائر الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says a bird’s wing-beating is its prayer and its voice is its glorification.
rows.anchor: ضرب الأجنحة صلاة الطير وصوته تسبيحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause may mean God knows each creature’s worship or each worshipper knows its own prayer and glorification.
rows.anchor: كل مصل ومسبح منهم قد علم صلاة نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God drives and joins clouds, piles them up, and rain emerges through them; wadq is rain and khilāl is their middle.
rows.anchor: بجمع بين قطع السحاب المتفرقة بعضها إلى بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Mountains of hail” may mean hail descending, with من extra, or an immense quantity like mountains.
rows.anchor: يعني: ينزل البرد، و"من" صلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the mountains as actual mountains of hail in the sky; Ibn ʿAbbās says they are there, with hail omitted as the object.
rows.anchor: أخبر الله عز وجل أن في السماء جبالا من برد

rows.speaker: أهل النحو
rows.claim: The three من particles mark origin, partitive meaning, and kind/material respectively.
rows.anchor: لابتداء الغاية، لأن ابتداء الإنزال من السماء، وقوله تعالى "من جبال" للتبعيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hail destroys crops and property, while God diverts it; lightning nearly blinds with its brightness.
rows.anchor: فيصيب به} يعني بالبرد {من يشاء} فيهلك زروعة وأمواله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads يذهب with initial yāʾ in ḍamma and hāʾ in kasra.
rows.anchor: بضم الياء وكسر الهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rejecters recognize only the “Merciful of Yamāma,” meaning the false prophet Musaylima.
rows.anchor: ما نعرف الرحمن إلا رحمن اليمامة، يعنون مسيلمة الكذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read يأمرنا, referring to Muhammad’s command; the others read تأمرنا, addressing Muhammad directly.
rows.anchor: لما يأمرنا محمد بالسجود له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being told to prostrate to the Merciful increases their aversion to religion and faith.
rows.anchor: لهم: "اسجدوا للرحمن" {نفورا} عن الدين والإيمان

rows.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: The constellations are great, visible stars.
rows.anchor: هي النجوم الكبار، سميت بروجا لظهورها

rows.speaker: عطية العوفي
rows.claim: The constellations are guarded castles, as in the verse about fortified towers.
rows.anchor: قصورا فيها الحرس

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: They are twelve zodiacal signs, the stations of the seven planets; each planet has houses among the signs.
rows.anchor: هي البروج الاثنا عشر التي هي منازل الكواكب السبعة السيارة

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: The signs are grouped into fiery, earthy, airy, and watery triplicities.
rows.anchor: مثلثة نارية، والثور والسنبلة والجدي مثلثة أرضية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lamp is the sun; Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read the plural, meaning stars.
rows.anchor: يعني الشمس، كما قال: "وجعل الشمس سراجا"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the plural reading, the moon is already included among the lamps but singled out for merit, like palm and pomegranate among fruits.
rows.anchor: والقمر قد دخل في "السرج" على قراءة من قرأ بالجمع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Night and day replace one another, letting a person make up worship missed in one during the other.
rows.anchor: خلفا وعوضا، يقوم أحدهما مقام صاحبه

rows.speaker: شقيق
rows.claim: A man told ʿUmar that he missed the night prayer; ʿUmar told him to make it up in the day.
rows.anchor: جاء رجل إلى عمر بن الخطاب، قال فاتتني الصلاة الليلة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Night and day differ as black and white.
rows.anchor: جعل هذا أسود وهذا أبيض

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: They replace each other in cycles of light and darkness and increase and decrease.
rows.anchor: إذا ذهب أحدهما جاء الآخر فهما يتعاقبان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamza reads يذكر with lighter consonants; the others read يتذكر with doubling, meaning reflect and take heed; Mujāhid says gratitude is for God’s blessing in both.
rows.anchor: بتخفيف الذال والكاف وضمها من الذكر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: “Or seek gratitude” means thanking the Lord for His blessing in both periods.
rows.anchor: شكر نعمة ربه عليه فيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God spreads the clouds as He wills, over a distance of a day, two days, or more.
rows.anchor: مسيرة يوم أو يومين وأكثر على من يشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kasafan means separate pieces, wadq rain, and khilāl the clouds’ middle; people rejoice when rain reaches them.
rows.anchor: ويجعله كسفا} قطعا متفرقة {فترى الودق} المطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before rain, people were despairing; وإن كانوا may mean “though they were” or “they were only despairing.”
rows.anchor: من قبله لمبلسين} أي آيسين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated “before it” may be emphatic, or the first reference may be rain and the second cloud formation; Ibn Masʿūd’s reading omits the repetition.
rows.anchor: الأولى ترجع إلى إنزال المطر، والثانية إلى إنشاء السحاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ḥijāzī, Basran, and Abū Bakr readings use the singular أثر; the others use plural آثار.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الحجاز، والبصرة، وأبو بكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s mercy is rain and its effect on the earth; Muqātil calls the effect vegetation.
rows.anchor: أراد برحمة الله: المطر، أي: انظر إلى حسن تأثيره في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The One who revives earth after death can revive the dead.
rows.anchor: إن ذلك لمحيي الموتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cold harmful wind yellows the crops after greenness, and people deny their past blessing; لظلوا means “they would become.”
rows.anchor: رأوا النبت والزرع مصفرا بعد الخضرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ضعف is read with ḍamma in Quraysh and fatḥa in Tamīm; it refers to a weak fluid, a sperm drop.
rows.anchor: فالضم لغة قريش، والفتح لغة تميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People move from infant weakness to youthful strength, then old-age weakness and gray hair; God creates as He wills and is knowing and powerful.
rows.anchor: بعد ضعف الطفولية شبابا، وهو وقت القوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At resurrection, polytheists swear they stayed in the world less than an hour because worldly life seems brief beside the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: استقلوا أجل الدنيا لما عاينوا الآخرة

rows.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
rows.claim: They say they remained in their graves for less than an hour.
rows.anchor: ما لبثوا في قبورهم غير ساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were turned away from truth in life; their false claim, like their denial of resurrection, is exposed by God’s decree.
rows.anchor: يصرفون عن الحق في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “In God’s book” may refer to prior divine knowledge or God’s ruling.
rows.anchor: فيما كتب الله لكم في سابق علمه من اللبث في القبور

rows.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل
rows.claim: A reordered reading means those who know God’s Book and believe say they remained until resurrection, citing the barzakh verse.
rows.anchor: فيه تقديم وتأخير معناه. وقال الذين أوتوا العلم في كتاب الله والإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They tell the deniers that this is the resurrection rejected in worldly life, when they did not know it would occur.
rows.anchor: فهذا يوم البعث ولكنكم كنتم لا تعلمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They cite the barzakh lasting until resurrection.
rows.anchor: ومن ورائهم برزخ إلى يوم يبعثون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paradise is the abode of lasting residence; its people have no hardship or fatigue.
rows.anchor: أي: لا يصيبنا فيها عناء ومشقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers are not killed to gain relief; alternatively, death is not decreed for them.
rows.anchor: لا يهلكون فيستريحوا كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads يُجزى in passive with “every” nominative; the other readers use first-person plural and make “every” accusative.
rows.anchor: "كل" رفع على غير تسمية الفاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يصطرخون means crying for help; the form comes from ṣarākh, a cry, and they ask to leave the Fire and replace their past deeds with good ones.
rows.anchor: من الصراخ، وهو الصياح، يقولون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reflection-time is identified as puberty; ʿAṭāʾ, Qatāda, and al-Kalbī say eighteen years, al-Ḥasan forty, and Ibn ʿAbbās sixty, transmitting from ʿAlī.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء وقتادة والكلبي: ثمان عشرة سنة

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet says God has excused a person whose life He extended to sixty years.
rows.anchor: أعذر الله تعالى إلى امرئ أخر أجله حتى بلغه ستين سنة

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet says the community’s lifespans range from sixty to seventy, with few exceeding that.
rows.anchor: أعمار أمتي ما بين الستين إلى السبعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most exegetes identify the warner as Muhammad; another view says the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: صلى الله عليه وسلم، هذا قول أكثر المفسرين

rows.speaker: عكرمة وسفيان بن عيينة ووكيع
rows.claim: The warner is gray hair: people were given time until gray, a sign warning of death.
rows.anchor: هو الشيب. معناه أو لم نعمركم حتى شبتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A transmitted saying has each white hair tell another to prepare because death is near.
rows.anchor: ما من شعرة تبيض إلا قالت لأختها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers are told to taste punishment because they have no helper.
rows.anchor: فذوقوا فما للظالمين من نصير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the unseen and what hearts contain.
rows.anchor: إنه عليم بذات الصدور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People succeed one another in the earth; alternatively, a later community witnessed former peoples and should learn from them.
rows.anchor: يخلف بعضكم بعضا، وقيل: جعلكم أمة خلفت من قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelief brings its consequence and increases only divine wrath and loss.
rows.anchor: ولا يزيد الكافرين كفرهم عند ربهم إلا مقتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza read ننكسه with doubling; the others read it lightly, meaning return to weak old age like a child.
rows.anchor: شبه الصبي في أول الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that limbs weaken after strength and return to decline.
rows.anchor: نضعف جوارحه بعد قوتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The One who changes human conditions can resurrect the dead.
rows.anchor: قدر على تصريف أحوال الإنسان يقدر على البعث بعد الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Meccan disbelievers called Muhammad a poet, but God did not teach him poetry and it did not come naturally.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: إن كفار مكة قالوا: إن محمدا شاعر، وما يقوله شعر

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: The Prophet recited a line in a variant order; Abū Bakr corrected the poet’s wording, and he and ʿUmar testified this confirmed his truthfulness.
rows.anchor: بهذا البيت: كفى بالإسلام والشيب للمرء ناهيا

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿĀʾisha said the Prophet sometimes recited verse by ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥa, including a line about unexpected news.
rows.anchor: كان يتمثل من شعر عبد الله بن رواحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God wanted a child, He could choose from creation what He willed; “what He creates” means angels, as in the verse about taking amusement.
rows.anchor: لاختار، {مما يخلق ما يشاء} يعني: الملائكة، كما قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is exalted above offspring and whatever is unworthy of His purity.
rows.anchor: تنزيها له عن ذلك، وعما لا يليق بطهارته

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Rolling night over day means one covers the other.
rows.anchor: يغشي هذا هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says one enters the other.
rows.anchor: يدخل أحدهما على الآخر

rows.speaker: الحسن والكلبي
rows.claim: Night decreases as day increases and vice versa; extremes are nine and fifteen hours. Takwīr means wrapping or gathering, as with a turban.
rows.anchor: أصل التكوير اللف والجمع، ومنه: كور العمامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sun and moon are governed, each running to an appointed term.
rows.anchor: كل يجري لأجل مسمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The single soul is Adam and his mate is Eve.
rows.anchor: يعني: آدم، {ثم جعل منها زوجها} يعني حواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Sending down” livestock means creating them; alternatives connect it to water producing cotton and fodder or making livestock provisions.
rows.anchor: معنى الإنزال هاهنا: الإحداث والإنشاء، كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eight pairs are species, explained in al-Anʿām.
rows.anchor: ثمانية أزواج} أصناف، تفسيرها في سورة الأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Womb creation proceeds from drop to clot to lump of flesh, as in Noah 14.
rows.anchor: نطفة ثم علقة ثم مضغة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The three darknesses are the abdomen, womb, and placenta.
rows.anchor: ظلمة البطن، وظلمة الرحم، وظلمة المشيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sincere worship means exclusive monotheism without associating anything with God.
rows.anchor: مخلصا له التوحيد لا أشرك به شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is commanded to be the first Muslim of this community.
rows.anchor: من هذه الأمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He fears punishment if he disobeys and worships another; this was when people called him to his fathers’ religion.
rows.anchor: قل إني أخاف إن عصيت ربي} وعبدت غيره، {عذاب يوم عظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Worship what you will” is threat and rebuke, as in the command to do as one wills.
rows.anchor: أمر توبيخ وتهديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The losers lose themselves and their families, meaning spouses and servants.
rows.anchor: أزواجهم وخدمهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: God assigned each person a Paradise home and family; the obedient receive theirs, while a sinner’s home passes to another.
rows.anchor: جعل لكل إنسان منزلا في الجنة وأهلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says the self is lost by entering Hell and family by separation.
rows.anchor: خسران النفس بدخول النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The upper canopies are layers of fire’s enclosures and smoke; lower ones are fiery bedding to the bottom.
rows.anchor: أطباق سرادقات من النار ودخانها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: God supports messengers and believers by victory and domination.
rows.anchor: بالغلبة والقهر

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: God supports them through proof in this life and acquittal in the next.
rows.anchor: بالحجة، وفي الآخرة بالعذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Support also comes through vengeance on enemies, proof, domination, destruction, or posthumous vengeance; angels witness that messengers conveyed and disbelievers denied.
rows.anchor: يشهدون للرسل بالتبليغ وعلى الكفار بالتكذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Excuses for disbelief will not be accepted; repentance will not benefit, and their abode is Hell.
rows.anchor: إن اعتذروا عن كفرهم لم يقبل منهم

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: The guidance given to Moses is the Torah and deliverance from error.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: الهدى من الضلالة، يعني التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad should be patient through harm because God’s promise to establish his religion and destroy enemies is true; seeking forgiveness raises his rank and models worship.
rows.anchor: وعد الله} في إظهار دينك وإهلاك أعدائك {حق

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: The fighting verse abrogated the patience verse.
rows.anchor: نسخت آية القتال آية الصبر

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Evening and morning means ʿAṣr and Fajr; Ibn ʿAbbās says it means the five prayers.
rows.anchor: صلاة العصر وصلاة الفجر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Their motive is arrogance toward Muhammad and hope to overcome him, which they will not attain because God will humiliate them.
rows.anchor: ما هم ببالغي ذلك

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The passage was revealed about Jews predicting that the Dajjāl, their supposed Messiah, would rule land and sea and restore their kingdom; God says to seek refuge from his trial.
rows.anchor: المسيح بن داود -يعنون الدجال-يخرج في آخر الزمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever God leaves astray has no protector to guide him or shield him from punishment; wrongdoers ask to return on seeing it.
rows.anchor: فما له من أحد يلي هدايته بعد إضلال الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condemned are shown the Fire, humbled, and steal furtive glances from fear and shame.
rows.anchor: خاشعين} خاضعين متواضعين، {من الذل ينظرون من طرف خفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “From a furtive glance” may mean because of humiliation, a weak hidden look, barely opening an eye, or looking with the heart because they are resurrected blind.
rows.anchor: لا يفتح عينه إنما ينظر ببعضها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers call them losers because the selves went to Hell and their families went to others in Paradise.
rows.anchor: بأن صاروا إلى النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They have no path to truth in this life or Paradise in the next; the path of good is closed.
rows.anchor: قد انسد عليهم طريق الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Responding to the Lord means answering His caller, Muhammad.
rows.anchor: أجيبوا داعي الله يعني محمدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day of Resurrection cannot be repelled; no refuge or denier can change what happens.
rows.anchor: لا يقدر أحد على دفعه وهو يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: The disbeliever makes his desired religion his god, following whatever he wants without fearing God or forbidding what God forbids.
rows.anchor: ذلك الكافر اتخذ دينه ما يهواه، فلا يهوى شيئا إلا ركبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view is that he worships whatever his desire inclines him toward.
rows.anchor: يعبد ما تهواه نفسه

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Arabs worshipped stones, gold, or silver, then broke or discarded one when they found a better object.
rows.anchor: كانت العرب يعبدون الحجارة والذهب والفضة

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Hawā is so called because it makes its companion fall into Hell.
rows.anchor: يهوي بصاحبه في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God misled the person knowing the outcome; alternatively, prior divine knowledge established his misguidance before creation.
rows.anchor: منه بعاقبة أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seal prevents hearing and understanding guidance; the eye’s covering prevents seeing guidance. Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read غشوة; others غشاوة.
rows.anchor: فلم يسمع الهدى، {وقلبه} فلم يعقل الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Deniers say worldly life alone exists: parents die and children live; time, long life, and the alternation of night and day destroy them, without knowledge.
rows.anchor: أي يموت الآباء ويحيا الأبناء

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A divine report forbids saying “woe to time”: God is Time, sends night and day, and may seize them at will.
rows.anchor: فإني أنا الدهر، أرسل الليل والنهار

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet forbids cursing time and calling grapes karm, saying God is Time and karm is the Muslim man.
rows.anchor: لا يسب أحدكم الدهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs blamed time for calamities; because God is the real agent, cursing time ultimately curses God, so they were forbidden.
rows.anchor: كانوا ينسبون إليه ما يصيبهم من المصائب والمكاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created heaven and earth without incapacity, so He can revive the dead.
rows.anchor: ولم يعي بخلقهن

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة والأخفش
rows.claim: The bāʾ in بقادر is extra for emphasis.
rows.anchor: الباء زائدة للتأكيد

rows.speaker: الكسائي والفراء
rows.claim: Arabs insert bāʾ in interrogatives with negation.
rows.anchor: العرب تدخل الباء في الاستفهام مع الجحد

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaʿqūb reads يقدر as a verb; Abū ʿUbayda prefers the common reading because ʿAbd Allāh reads قادر without bāʾ.
rows.anchor: في قراءة عبد الله قادر بغير باء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers affirm the Fire is real and are told to taste punishment for their disbelief.
rows.anchor: فذوقوا العذاب بما كنتم تكفرون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The possessors of resolve are people of firmness.
rows.anchor: ذوو الحزم

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: They are people of seriousness and patience.
rows.anchor: ذوو الجد والصبر

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: All messengers had resolve and judgment; “from” indicates kind rather than a subset.
rows.anchor: كل الرسل كانوا أولي عزم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other lists identify them as all except Jonah, the eighteen named in al-Anʿām, those ordered to fight, six named in other sūrahs, or six exemplars of patience.
rows.anchor: إلا يونس بن متى، لعجلة كانت منه

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: His six are Noah, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, and Job, each enduring a distinct trial.
rows.anchor: نوح، صبر على أذى قومه، وإبراهيم، صبر على النار

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: They are the five lawgivers: Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad.
rows.anchor: هم نوح، وإبراهيم، وموسى، وعيسى، أصحاب الشرائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author supports the five by the verses specifying the covenant-bearing prophets and the religion prescribed to Noah.
rows.anchor: وإذ أخذنا من النبيين ميثاقهم ومنك ومن نوح

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: The Prophet says this world is unfit for him and his family, and God required from him the patience required of the possessors of resolve.
rows.anchor: إن الله لم يرض من أولي العزم إلا بالصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad should not hasten the punishment; he may have grown impatient for it to fall on those who refused.
rows.anchor: فإنه نازل بهم لا محالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When they see the punishment, worldly and grave residence seems like an hour because the past seems not to have existed.
rows.anchor: صار طول لبثهم في الدنيا والبرزخ كأنه ساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “A proclamation” means the Qur’an and its explanation are a message from God.
rows.anchor: هذا القرآن وما فيه من البيان بلاغ من الله إليكم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Only transgressors perish under God’s mercy and grace; some call this the strongest verse for hope.
rows.anchor: ما في الرجاء لرحمة الله آية أقوى من هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the heavens, earth, and what is between in six days without fatigue.
rows.anchor: لغوب} ، إعياء وتعب. نزلت في اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse answers Jews who claimed God rested on Saturday after creation; the Prophet recounted the six-day sequence, and God refuted their claim.
rows.anchor: ثم استراح يوم السبت، واستلقى على العرش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience through their denial was commanded before the command to fight.
rows.anchor: وهذا قبل الأمر بقتالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Glorifying God with praise means prayer in gratitude; before sunrise is Fajr and before sunset ʿAṣr.
rows.anchor: يعني: صلاة الصبح، {وقبل الغروب} ، يعني: صلاة العصر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: “Before sunset” means Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr.
rows.anchor: الظهر والعصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night glorification means Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ; Mujāhid says any night prayer.
rows.anchor: ومن الليل فسبحه} ، يعني: صلاة المغرب والعشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥijāzī readers and Ḥamza read إدبار with kasra as a verbal noun; others read أدبار with fatḥa as a plural.
rows.anchor: مصدر أدبر إدبارا، وقرأ الآخرون بفتحها على جمع الدبر

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب وعلي بن أبي طالب والحسن والشعبي والنخعي والأوزاعي
rows.claim: “After prostrations” is two rakʿahs after Maghrib; “after stars” is two before Fajr, the majority view.
rows.anchor: "أدبار السجود" الركعتان بعد صلاة المغرب، وأدبار النجوم الركعتان قبل صلاة الفجر

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: The Prophet maintained the two rakʿahs before dawn more consistently than any other voluntary prayer; he also said they are better than the world.
rows.anchor: أشد معاهدة منه على الركعتين أمام الصبح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most exegetes take فلا أقسم as “I swear,” with لا extra; ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar reads فلأقسم with explicit hamza.
rows.anchor: معناه: أقسم و"لا" صلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, لا rebuts the disbelievers’ claim that the Qur’an is magic, poetry, or soothsaying before beginning the oath.
rows.anchor: رد لما قاله الكفار في القرآن إنه سحر وشعر وكهانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read “position” singular; others read “positions” plural.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي: "بموقع" على التوحيد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The locations are the stars of Qur’anic revelation, since it descended in installments.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أراد نجوم القرآن، فإنه كان ينزل على رسول الله

rows.speaker: جماعة من المفسرين
rows.claim: The locations are star settings and places of descent; ʿAṭāʾ says their stations, and al-Ḥasan says their scattering at resurrection.
rows.anchor: مغارب النجوم ومساقطها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tremendous oath magnifies the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: وإنه لقسم لو تعلمون عظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to the Qur’an, the object of the oath.
rows.anchor: يعني هذا الكتاب وهو موضع القسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is noble and honored because it is God’s speech; noble can mean giving abundant good.
rows.anchor: عزيز مكرم لأنه كلام الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hidden book is the Preserved Tablet with God, protected from devils.
rows.anchor: في اللوح المحفوظ، محفوظ من الشياطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly life’s play has no lasting result, amusement passes, adornment is appearance, and people boast and compete in wealth and children.
rows.anchor: لعب} باطل لا حاصل له {ولهو} فرح ثم ينقضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The life is like rain whose growth impresses farmers, then dries, yellows, and breaks apart.
rows.anchor: أعجب الكفار} أي: الزراع {نباته} ما نبت من ذلك الغيث

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: The severe punishment is for God’s enemies; forgiveness and approval are for His allies and obedient people.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: لأعداء الله {ومغفرة من الله ورضوان}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transient harvest shows worldly life is deceptive enjoyment.
rows.anchor: يتحطم ويتكسر بعد يبسه ويفنى

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Worldly life is delusive enjoyment for one occupied in it while seeking the Hereafter; used as a means, it carries one toward what is better.
rows.anchor: متاع الغرور لمن يشتغل فيها بطلب الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Tomorrow” means resurrection; each person should examine what he has sent ahead, righteous deeds that save or bad deeds that ruin.
rows.anchor: يعني ليوم القيامة، أي: لينظر أحدكم أي شيء قدم لنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows what people do.
rows.anchor: إن الله خبير بما تعملون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who forgot God abandoned His command, so God made them forget their interests and fail to prepare good for themselves.
rows.anchor: تركوا أمر الله {فأنساهم أنفسهم}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wealth and children must not distract from remembrance, meaning the five prayers; compare those not distracted by trade.
rows.anchor: يعني الصلوات الخمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever is distracted from remembrance by wealth and children is a loser.
rows.anchor: من شغله ماله وولده عن ذكر الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The commanded spending means zakat on wealth.
rows.anchor: يريد زكاة الأموال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At death a person asks for a short reprieve to give charity and become righteous, meaning a believer.
rows.anchor: فأتصدق وأزكي مالي، {وأكن من الصالحين}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may express a wish, with لا treated as extra.
rows.anchor: وقيل: "لا" صلة، فيكون الكلام بمعنى التمني

rows.speaker: مقاتل وجماعة
rows.claim: One view says the verse concerns hypocrites; another says believers. Righteousness here may mean pilgrimage; Ibn ʿAbbās says one who dies owing zakat and able to perform Hajj asks to return.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالصلاح هنا: الحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads وأكون with wāw and subjunctive as a response to the wish; others read jussive وأكن, coordinated with فأصدق and written without wāw.
rows.anchor: على جواب التمني وعلى لفظ فأصدق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Bakr reads يعملون in third person; the others read تعملون in second person.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو بكر: "يعملون" بالياء وقرأ الآخرون بالتاء

none: Qur'an text only; no commentary is included in this segment.
